definition: In cognition, dilation usually means temporal dilation: a change in time perception in which an event or stimulus is experienced as lasting longer than it actually does. In the supplied source, this effect is described as being strengthened by increased arousal.

reasons: The definition claims that, in cognition, dilation “usually means temporal dilation,” but the packet only discusses temporal dilation in the specific context of facial attractiveness and time perception; it does not support a general “usually” meaning.

The claim about the effect being strengthened/mediated by increased arousal is supported by the packet (Experiment 1: increased arousal mediated temporal dilation; Experiment 2: downregulating arousal attenuated it).

The packet supports a specific finding about the temporal dilation effect of attractive faces, but it does not support the broad dictionary-style generalization that “dilation” usually means this in cognition.
The phrase “experienced as lasting longer than it actually does” is not stated in the source and goes beyond the packet’s wording.

The source supports a relationship in which increased arousal mediates or underlies the temporal dilation effect, but not the stronger general claim that dilation is generally “strengthened by increased arousal” across cognition.
